text:
sam: Quick handoff — taking off for the night at 01:00 UTC, handing oncall to @maya. Heads-up: small prod deploy scheduled at 01:30 UTC (config + small index tweak). Expect ~5–10% traffic canary for 20m then full rollout if green.

maya: Got it — will take over. Can you drop the deploy checklist and rollback steps here? :eyes:

sam: Sure — checklist summary:
- Preflight: migration dry-run on staging ✅
- Health checks: readiness probes, DB connections validated ✅
- Canary: 5% for 20m, smoke tests run via smoke-runner job
- Rollback plan: immediate flag flip or kube undo

sam: Rollback commands (if needed):
```bash
# flip feature flag immediately
curl -X POST "$FLAG_SERVICE/internal/toggle" -d '{"flag":"new_index","state":false}'
# or kubernetes rollback for api-service
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/api-service
```

kevin: Do we need any extra watchers on infra? I'm around until 02:15 UTC and can monitor GPU pools and routing. Otherwise ping me.

maya: Thanks @kevin — can you watch the routing + capacity dashboards during canary? I'll focus on logs and error rates.

ravi: FYI there's a minor latency blip seen in staging last run (~120ms tail) when sequence length >1200. Not expected to affect this deploy but keeping in notes. If latency >200ms during canary, we abort.

deploy-bot: Canary job started — 5% traffic | batch-id=canary-1972223333 | started_at=1972223600

maya: Nice. Running smoke tests now, will post results. If smoke passes and no error rate regressions >0.5% relative, I'll promote.

sam: Also: freeze window 01:15–03:00 UTC for non-emergency changes. Only urgent rollbacks or mitigations during freeze.

maya: Copy that. I'll keep the runbook open: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/deploys/night-deploys — will reference rollback playbook if needed.

kevin: One ask — if we need to scale down canary due to infra pressure use this command: `rtctl set-weight api-service canary 1` to reduce to near zero quickly.

maya: Noted. If I see error spikes I'll reduce weight to 0 and notify.

ravi: Adding a quick telemetry check script I'll run every 5m during canary: `./scripts/check_telemetry.sh canary-1972223333` — will paste results if anything odd.

maya: Smoke results: all core endpoints OK, 200/200. No obvious schema errors. Proceeding.

deploy-bot: Canary metrics: error_rate=0.12% | avg_latency_ms=72 | error_budget_usage=0.8%

maya: Good. Proceeding to 25% now over next 10m, then full if stable. Will call out before final promote.

sam: Thanks team — briefed the support rotation too: support oncall will be on slack for the first 30m after full rollout. @maya you'll be primary if anything pages.

maya: Acknowledged. I'll keep monitoring and will escalate to @kevin or @sam if we hit the abort threshold.

kevin: I'll stay near my laptop for the first 20m after full rollout — reachable on mobile.

oncall-bot: Reminder: If any page fires, follow the incident checklist: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/incident  — create an incident channel and tag #incidents.

maya: Closing loop: canary -> 25% -> 100% complete, no regressions observed. Rolling back only if latency >200ms or error_rate jumps >0.5%. I'll post a final confirmation when 100% is live. :thumbsup:

sam: Perfect. Enjoy the evening everyone. Thanks for the coverage.

maya: 100% rollout done at ~1972224600. No issues observed. Logging handoff note in the oncall doc.

ravi: Logged telemetry snapshot to the deploy ticket. All looks normal.

kevin: Back to offline. ping if anything. :wave:
